article.title: Run into
article.description: Meaning 1: to meet someone unexpectedly. Example: 'I ran into an old friend at the mall.' Meaning 2: to encounter a problem. Example: 'We ran into some issues with the schedule.' Grammar note: inseparable phrasal verb — the object always comes after 'into'.
article.content: Meaning 1: to meet someone unexpectedly. Example: 'I ran into an old friend at the mall.' Meaning 2: to encounter a problem. Example: 'We ran into some issues with the schedule.' Grammar note: inseparable phrasal verb — the object always comes after 'into'.

generated.caption:
Ever met someone unexpectedly or faced a sudden problem? That's exactly when you'd use 'run into'!

This versatile phrasal verb means either to meet someone by chance (e.g., 'I ran into an old friend at the mall') OR to encounter an issue (e.g., 'We ran into some issues with the schedule'). Keep practicing!

slides.headlineRest: — Two Meanings You Need To Know
slides.body: The versatile phrasal verb "run into" has two primary meanings. Firstly, it means to meet someone unexpectedly, like when you bump into an acquaintance. For example: "I ran into an old friend at the mall." Secondly, "run into" signifies encountering a problem or difficulty, as in: "We ran into some issues with the schedule." Keep in mind that "run into" is an inseparable phrasal verb, meaning the object always comes after 'into'.
